pied.avertissement: Demonstration prototype. Your data stays in this browser: nothing is transmitted, no message is actually delivered, no contact is ever contacted. This is not a will in the legal sense — no disposal of property, no value in matters of inheritance.

accueil.accroche: Write, while you are alive, what you wish to pass on. Testament delivers it after your passing — established by a protocol, never by a mere inactivity timer.
accueil.intro1: A forgotten password, a long illness, a lost phone: none of these should ever send your messages. The service first reaches out to you over several channels, then asks the trusted people you have named, and only presumes your death at the end of delays you know in advance. Even then, ninety days of grace stand between that presumption and the slightest delivery.
accueil.intro2: This demonstration runs entirely in your browser. A test bench at the bottom of the screen lets you move time forward by months, so you can watch the protocol unfold.
accueil.boutonReprendre: Pick up where I left off
accueil.avertissementTitre: This is not a will in the legal sense.
accueil.avertissement: Testament passes on words, not an estate: no disposal of property, no bequest, no value in matters of inheritance. The service does not certify a death; it presumes it at the end of a protocol (BR-J-02).

menu.tableau: What the service knows about you, and the two dates that matter: if no one does anything, and at the earliest.
menu.messages: Write, seal, choose the recipients and the moment of delivery.
menu.contacts: Name the people who will be able to attest your death — without ever seeing your messages.
menu.public: Schedule an open letter, even during your lifetime, always reviewed by a human.

accueil.guideIntro: Six steps to understand the service in a few minutes.

1.texte: Under “Messages”, write a text, add an introductory note and one or more recipients. A draft never leaves: only a sealed message can be delivered.

2.texte: Two accepting people are enough to form a quorum. They see neither your messages nor your recipients; without them, the delay stretches to about twenty-one months.

3.texte: The protocol only runs once the account is armed: at least one sealed message, two-factor authentication, two verified contact channels, and your explicit consent.

4.texte: The test bench at the bottom of the screen jumps from one day to one year. Watch the check-in requests, the inquiry among your contacts, the presumption, then the grace period. “I am here” cancels everything, at any moment before execution.

5.texte: Once execution has begun, the “Recipients” section lets you open each envelope as a loved one would: a note, a waiting period if the message is difficult, and the freedom to open it later, or never.

6.titre: Stay in control of your data
6.texte: “My data” shows what will be kept or destroyed, lets you export the whole account in an open format, and delete it with a cooling-off period.

accueil.lexiqueTitre: A few words of the protocol

preuveDeVie.definition: A strong sign from you (signing in, a signed link) resets every counter. A weak sign, such as opening an email, only delays the escalation.

scelle.definition: The settled version of a message, the only one that can be delivered. It remains editable during your lifetime: the last sealed version prevails.

quorum.definition: Two attestations from distinct accepting contacts — or a single one, with supporting evidence, if you have only one contact.

presomption.definition: The conclusion of the protocol, never a certification: in the absence of any sign of life, and in view of the attestations or of an eighteen-month floor.

grace.definition: Ninety days, which cannot be shortened, between the presumption and delivery, during which a single sign of life cancels everything.

pli.definition: Everything a recipient receives, gathered into a single delivery: no one receives two notifications for the same passing.

banc.definition: The demonstration tool that moves time forward. It does not exist in the real service.

tableau.sous: What the service knows about you, and what would happen if you never came back.
tableau.alertePresumeTitre: Your messages will be delivered on {date}.
tableau.alertePresume: You are presumed deceased. A single click cancels the whole process and the counter starts again from zero (BR-C-03).
tableau.alerteJoindreTitre: We are trying to reach you.
tableau.alerteJoindre: Without a sign of life from you, the inquiry among your trusted contacts will continue.
tableau.aucunScelle: No sealed message: nothing will leave. Drafts are never delivered (BR-B-03).
tableau.auPlusTot: At the earliest, if your contacts attest
tableau.pasDeCheminCourt: no accepting contact: no shorter path
tableau.quorumPiece: quorum possible only with supporting evidence
tableau.quorumImpossible: quorum impossible: delay extended to 21 months
tableau.conseilContactsTitre: With two trusted contacts, your messages could leave about 12 months after your last visit; without them, the wait is 21 months (6-month cadence).
tableau.conseilContacts: A contact never has access to your messages (BR-A-12) and can trigger nothing alone (BR-A-14).
tableau.noteCheckin: In the real product, an authenticated sign-in counts as proof of life (S1). Here, the check-in is explicit so that the protocol can be observed.

armement.decouverteTitre: First visit? Explore everything in thirty seconds.
armement.decouverte: Load a sample account: two sealed messages, two trusted contacts, a scheduled open letter. You can then move time forward from the test bench, at the bottom of the screen, and watch the protocol unfold.
armement.sous: Until the account is armed, no protocol runs and nothing can be delivered (BR-C-01).
armement.pasJuridiqueTitre: This is not a will in the legal sense.
armement.pasJuridique: No disposal of property, no bequest, no value in matters of inheritance: the service passes on words, not an estate. It does not certify your death; it presumes it, at the end of a protocol you choose (BR-J-02).
armement.cond2faAide: Required for arming, not for signing up, so as not to discourage registration (BR-A-02, R-A-3).
armement.condCanauxAide: The protocol relies on redundancy: a single channel renders it ineffective (BR-A-03).
armement.nomAffichage: Display name — a pseudonym is allowed
armement.nomAide: This is the name your recipients will see. No directory, no search between users (BR-A-09).
armement.cadenceQuestion: How often do you agree to be asked?
armement.cadenceAide: The shorter the cadence, the faster the delivery after an actual death — and the more often you are asked during your lifetime.
armement.accuse: I have read and understood the protocol: check-in requests, inquiry among my contacts, presumption of death, then 90 days of grace before delivery (BR-C-02).

messages.sous: A draft is never delivered, whatever the state of the account (BR-B-03). A sealed message remains editable during your lifetime: only the last sealed version will leave (BR-B-05).

editeur.sousScelle: Sealed on {scelle} — deliverable from {executable} (BR-B-09). Any change will require sealing again.
editeur.sousBrouillon: Draft — it will not leave until it is sealed.
editeur.titreInterne: Internal title (only you can see it, BR-B-02)
editeur.noteExemple: Shown to the recipient before they open the message
editeur.noteAide: This is the only text the recipient will see before opening. The content itself never appears in a notification (BR-D-08).
editeur.fortImpact: This message is hard to receive (a revelation, a confession, a reproach). The recipient will have a reinforced threshold and 24 hours to reflect before being able to open it (BR-B-08, BR-D-13).
editeur.aucunDestinataire: No recipient: the message cannot be sealed.
editeur.jamaisAverti: The recipient is never told during the lifetime of the testator (BR-B-11).
editeur.groupeAide: A group is a named list: each person receives their own access, never as a copy visible to the others (BR-B-15).
editeur.rendrePublic: Make this message public — anyone on the platform will be able to read it, after review by a human moderator. Without this box, the message remains strictly private.
editeur.confirmePublic: I confirm: once published, this text may be read, quoted and copied by anyone, and I will no longer be able to control what becomes of it.
editeur.datePublication: Publication date — may fall during your lifetime (BR-B-18)
editeur.datePublicationAide: Nothing is ever put online automatically: on that date, the message goes to human review, and a moderator decides (BR-D-15). Target: seven days.
editeur.indexable: Allow search engines to index this message. This box is deliberately separate from the permission to publish (BR-D-19).
editeur.directive: After my account is deleted, these words will be… (BR-E-03)
editeur.directiveAide: A text that identifies you by itself (“I, mayor of…”) cannot be anonymised: the anonymous archive will refuse it rather than pretend (BR-E-04).
editeur.dateDelivrance: Date (if a specific date, up to 25 years ahead — BR-B-19)

contacts.sous: People able to attest your death. They have access to nothing: not your messages, not your recipients, not even how many there are (BR-A-12). And none of them can trigger anything alone — it takes two (BR-A-14).
contacts.aucun: No contact named. Without a contact, your messages will leave at the earliest 21 months after your last visit, against about 12 with two (6-month cadence).
contacts.acceptationAide: Until a person has explicitly accepted, they do not count towards the quorum (BR-A-11). Here, acceptance is simulated with a click; in the real product, it goes through a verified link.
contacts.executeurIntro: One of your contacts may be given supervisory powers — one by one, none by default. They will never be able to read a message, create one, change one, or add a recipient (BR-A-20). They oversee the mechanism; they do not reach the substance.

pouvoirs.SUSPENSION: Permanently suspend a message before it is delivered — the only destructive power, to be granted only with full awareness (BR-A-22)
pouvoirs.COORDONNEES: Provide a recipient’s missing contact details

contacts.dabordAcceptant: First name an accepting trusted contact.

plis.aucune: This page appears once execution has begun.
plis.pouvoirsAccordes: Powers granted: {liste}. They can neither read, nor change, nor add a recipient (BR-A-20).
plis.fenetreReport: Notified on {prevenu}, they may postpone until {jusquau} (BR-D-05).

reportee.one: Execution postponed by one month on {date}.

plis.sous: One envelope per recipient, gathering all their messages: no one receives two notifications for the same deceased (BR-D-03). The trusted contacts were notified on {date}, seven days before the recipients, so that a human being can break the news before the machine does (A-7).

sas.signature: Message left by {nom}, last modified on {date}. You may keep it: download it, as it will remain online for only twelve months.
sas.plusValide: This link is no longer valid
sas.destine: A message is meant for you
sas.desoles: We are sorry that you should learn of it this way, if you did not already know. There is no hurry: this message will wait for you. You may open it today, in a month, or never.
sas.difficileTitre: This message is hard to receive.
sas.reflexion24h: You are given 24 hours to reflect: you will be able to open it from {date}.
sas.prenezLeTemps: Take all the time you need; bereavement support resources are available.
sas.codeDemo: For this demonstration, the code is shown: {code}
sas.refuser: I do not wish to receive it

public.demandeTiers: Removal request from a person mentioned
public.sous: A public message can be scheduled for a date you choose — even during your lifetime (BR-B-18). But nothing is ever put online automatically: when the date comes, the text goes to human review, and a moderator decides (BR-D-15).
public.consoleTitre: Moderation console — the service’s role, not yours
public.consoleAide: This queue would not exist in the testator’s real application: it is shown here to make the rule observable. Every decision is named and reasoned (BR-M-03), and a refusal deletes nothing silently: the message switches to private, towards your trusted contacts, with the reason (BR-D-17).

donnees.sous: What the service keeps, what it destroys, and when. Four sets with different fates: your account, the messages still to come, what has been published, and the log of decisions.
donnees.suppression: It will become final on {date}. Until then, you can still change your mind — this 72-hour delay exists to protect you against a takeover of your mailbox (BR-A-06).
donnees.e2Aide: kept outside the account, until their date
donnees.e4Aide: facts and dates only, kept for 5 years
donnees.e2Titre: E2 — what will outlive my account (BR-B-20)
donnees.e2Explication: A message scheduled for a distant date is kept in a separate store, reduced to the bare minimum: the text, the recipient, the date. An incident affecting the rest of the account cannot take it away.
donnees.e3Titre: E3 — my public messages after me
donnees.e3Explication: The fate of each public message is chosen during your lifetime, in the message editor. No setting sends anything to the archive by default (BR-E-03), and a text that still identifies you by itself cannot be falsely anonymised (BR-E-04).
donnees.export: An open folder, readable without this service: your messages as text and HTML, and a JSON index of everything else.
donnees.supprimer: Immediate, apart from a 72-hour cooling-off period. All undelivered messages are destroyed — permanently.

journal.sous: Every decision, automatic or human, leaves a time-stamped and chained trace: it is the only possible defence in the event of a dispute (PD-7, BR-C-10).

invites.pause: Planned absence for how many months? (1 to 12)
invites.pouvoirSuspension: The power of suspension is irreversible: your executor will be able to destroy a message before it leaves — for instance one meant for someone they dislike. Grant it?
invites.reporter: Postpone execution by how many months? (1 to 12)
invites.confirmerSuspension: Confirm the suspension? The message will be destroyed and will never leave.
invites.reflexion: Your reflection — it will go through human review before becoming visible:
invites.categorie: Category: HAINE (hatred), HARCELEMENT (harassment), CONTENU_ILLICITE (unlawful content), ATTEINTE_VIE_PRIVEE (privacy), AUTRE (other)
invites.supprimerCompte: Request permanent deletion of the account? You will have 72 hours to change your mind.
invites.motifRefus: Reason for refusal (required, it will be communicated):
invites.motifTiers: Reason given by the person mentioned:
invites.remplacerExemple: Replace the current data with a sample set?
invites.toutEffacer: Erase all local data and start again from zero?

notifs.cocherConfirmation: Also tick the confirmation: a public publication is, in practice, irreversible (BR-B-16).
notifs.checkin: Proof of life recorded: the counter starts again from zero and any process under way is cancelled.

pause.one: Planned absence of one month: the protocol is suspended, nothing can be triggered.
pause.other: Planned absence of {n} months: the protocol is suspended, nothing can be triggered.

notifs.lireProtocole: You must confirm that you have read the protocol (BR-C-02).
notifs.arme: Account armed. The proof-of-life protocol runs from now on.
notifs.exempleRapide: Sample account loaded. Move time forward from the test bench, at the bottom.
notifs.brouillon: Draft saved. It will not leave until it is sealed.
notifs.scelle: Message sealed (version {n}). It will become deliverable on {date} — a 24-hour delay (BR-B-09).
notifs.destinataireAjoute: Recipient added. They will never be told during your lifetime (BR-B-11).
notifs.groupeAjoute: Group added. Delivery will remain individual (BR-B-15).
notifs.invitation: Invitation sent. The contact must accept it explicitly to count (BR-A-11).
notifs.contactRefus: Refusal recorded: this third party’s data is purged immediately.
notifs.contactRenonce: Withdrawal recorded: you are informed without delay (BR-A-13).
notifs.codeEnvoye: A one-time code has just been sent — no account creation is required (BR-D-10).
notifs.messageOuvert: Message opened. Your reading is recorded, but disclosed to no one (BR-D-12).
notifs.plusTard: Reminder in three months. No reminder will be sent to you in the meantime.
notifs.pliRefuse: Refusal recorded. The message is kept for twelve months in case you change your mind (BR-D-11).
notifs.telecharge: Message downloaded: it now belongs to you, outside the service.
notifs.rebond: Permanent bounce simulated: 3 new attempts over 30 days, then a switch to the backup recipient (BR-D-07).
notifs.executeurDesigne: Executor appointed. Each power was granted explicitly — none is granted by default (BR-A-18).
notifs.executeurRetire: Role removed. The powers disappear with it.

reportee.one: Execution postponed by one month. The other contacts are informed (BR-A-21).
reportee.other: Execution postponed by {n} months. The other contacts are informed (BR-A-21).

notifs.suspensionDemandee: Suspension requested. It requires confirmation 48 hours later, and will be irreversible (BR-A-22).
notifs.canalRepare: Channel repaired: the recipient does not change, only their address is corrected (BR-A-19 c).
notifs.reflexionDeposee: Reflection left. It will only appear after human review (BR-D-21).
notifs.reflexionsReglees: Reflections setting changed. After execution, it will become final (BR-D-23).
notifs.signalement: Report recorded. Serious categories are handled within 24 hours (BR-D-25).
notifs.signalementClasse: Report closed without action, and logged.

export.one: Export of {n} message and of the log — open format (BR-E-07).
export.other: Export of {n} messages and of the log — open format (BR-E-07).

notifs.suppressionDemandee: Deletion requested. It will become final in 72 hours — move time forward to see it carried out.
notifs.suppressionAnnulee: Deletion cancelled. Nothing has been destroyed.
notifs.publie: Message published after human review. No publication is ever automatic (BR-D-15).
notifs.refusMotive: Reasoned refusal. The message is not deleted: it switches to private, towards your trusted contacts (BR-D-17).
notifs.detresse: Alert raised: support resources are offered to the author, who is alive (§7.4).
notifs.retraitTiers: Request recorded: priority handling, target 72 hours (BR-D-20).
notifs.s2SansEffet: Weak signal with no effect here — an S2 never resets the counter (BR-C-04).
notifs.s2: Email opened without authentication: escalation postponed by 30 days, counter unchanged (BR-C-04).
notifs.aucunAttestant: No accepting contact available to attest.
notifs.atteste: {nom} attests the death. Two are needed for a quorum (BR-A-14) — or a single one with evidence if you have only one contact.
notifs.exempleCharge: Sample set loaded: account armed, two sealed messages, two accepting contacts.

exemple.m1Texte:
Nour,

There are three things I never managed to tell you face to face.

The first is that on the day you were born, I was afraid — not of you, of myself.
exemple.m1Note: A letter written on a Sunday in January.
exemple.m2Texte:
Sami,

There is something our family kept from you for forty years.
exemple.m2Note: This message contains a family revelation.
exemple.m3Titre: Open letter — published during my lifetime
exemple.m3Texte:
To whoever will kindly read it.

I waited forty years to write these lines, and I decided not to wait for my death for them to be read.

demo.sous: Simulator of the proof-of-life protocol — specification v0.1, sections 4 and 5
demo.initial: Account armed on {date} (cadence 6 months), 2 sealed messages, contacts Awa and Bilal accepting.
demo.okS1: S1 check-in (signed link): counter reset to zero, any process cancelled (BR-C-03).
demo.s2SansEffet: S2 with no effect here: the counter never moves (BR-C-04).
demo.okS2: S2 (email opened): escalation postponed by 30 days, counter unchanged (BR-C-04).
demo.okS2exp: “I am alive”: presumption cancelled, S1 check-in requested again (Phase 4).
demo.okPause: Planned absence of 3 months: protocol suspended (BR-C-07).
demo.okVivant: Awa answers “all is well”: escalation suspended for 60 days (only once).
demo.okAwa: Awa attests the death (with evidence): named attestation recorded (BR-A-17).
demo.okBilal: Bilal attests the death: the quorum of 2 can be reached (BR-A-14).
demo.sasFortImpact: — high impact: 24 h to reflect before opening (BR-D-13)
demo.lu: Read: “{texte}” — reading recorded, disclosed to no one (BR-D-12).
demo.tard: “Later”: reminder requested in 3 months. No unsolicited reminder in the meantime (§7.3).
demo.refus: Final refusal: content kept for 12 months just in case, then erased (BR-D-11).
demo.m1Texte: Nour, three things I never managed to tell you…
demo.m2Texte: Sami, there is something you need to know about our family.
demo.m2Note: This message contains a family revelation.
